metaDescription: Six pressure washers at or under $500, including 3300 and 3400 PSI gas models and the highest-flow electrics, compared on pumps, engines and cleaning units.
expertTake: The DeWalt DXPW3300 gas washer is the best overall pick because its 208cc engine and 2.4 GPM pump deliver the flow that driveways and decks need. The Greenworks 3000 PSI brushless is the pick for electric users, with lab-verified figures. If you only wash cars and furniture, nothing in this band is worth the extra money over the lower tiers.
introParagraphs: This is the band where gas washers appear, and the difference they make is flow. A gas machine moves more than twice the water of a typical electric unit, which is why it strips a driveway in minutes while an electric takes an afternoon.
The trade is noise, fuel and upkeep. Prices move, and the $500 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: DeWalt DXPW3300 3300 PSI 2.4 GPM Gas Pressure Washer
products.description:
The DXPW3300 pairs a 208cc DeWalt engine with an axial cam pump rated at 3300 PSI and 2.4 GPM, which is about 7,920 cleaning units. That is more than triple the best electric washer in the lower price tiers, and it is why gas machines clean concrete so much faster. The engine must be able to drive the pump, and a 208cc class engine is a reasonable match for 2.4 GPM at this pressure.

It has a welded steel frame and 10-inch pneumatic tires, so it rolls over uneven ground. The axial cam pump is economical and suited to occasional use, but unlike a triplex plunger pump it is generally not rebuildable, so it is a consumable if abused or frozen.

Ownership means gas engine care: fresh stabilized fuel, an oil change each season, a clean air filter and a good spark plug. Never run the pump dry, and winterize with pump antifreeze. It is the right choice for a homeowner with a driveway, deck and fence to maintain. Before the first start, check the engine oil level, because many gas washers ship with the crankcase dry or low. Connect the water supply and squeeze the trigger until water runs steadily before pulling the cord, which keeps the pump from running dry.
products.bestFor: Driveways, decks and siding on a single machine.
pros: Flow of 2.4 GPM cleans concrete quickly
Welded steel frame and pneumatic tires
cons: Gas engine needs fuel and oil upkeep

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3400 3400 PSI 2.6 GPM Gas Pressure Washer

specList.label: Kit
specList.value: Onboard soap tank, 25 ft hose, 5 nozzles

products.description:
The WPX3400 states slightly higher pressure and flow than the DeWalt, 3400 PSI at 2.6 GPM, giving about 8,840 cleaning units. It runs a 212cc four-stroke overhead-valve engine with recoil start and ships with an onboard soap tank, a 25 foot super-flex hose, a spray gun and a five-nozzle set.

The extra pressure and flow are a modest edge, roughly 12 percent on cleaning units, and the difference in daily use is small. The broader kit and the known Westinghouse engine line make it the stronger value when the price is lower, while the DeWalt brings a better-known name for service.

As with any gas washer, use fresh fuel, change the oil, clean the air filter and winterize the pump. It suits a homeowner who wants maximum claimed power for the money. Because it ships with a soap tank and five nozzles, you can wash a car and strip a fence with the same machine. Pick the wide tips for paint and wood, and keep the 0 degree tip for stubborn spots on concrete.
products.bestFor: Maximum power for large driveways and decks.
pros: Highest pressure and flow in the group
Onboard soap tank and five nozzles

products.name: Greenworks 3000 PSI Brushless Electric Pressure Washer 2.0 GPM Max

specList.label: Verification
specList.value: Pressure and flow verified by independent lab

products.description:
The Greenworks is the strongest electric in this list, with a 14 amp TruBrushless motor and a stated 3000 PSI and 2.0 GPM maximum. The maker says its pressure and flow claims were verified by an independent lab, which is the kind of statement worth looking for on any washer.

The JETTFLOW design is said to deliver up to 50 percent more flow, but remember that maximum figures are peaks. A 2.0 GPM maximum is still far below the gas washers' 2.4 to 2.6 GPM sustained, and the peak pressure and peak flow may not occur together.

It avoids the gas-engine chores entirely: no fuel, no oil, no plug and no pull cord. Drain the pump before freezing weather. It is the pick for someone who wants strong electric performance without an engine. Since the numbers are lab verified, you can plan a job with fair confidence: a 200 square foot deck is a manageable afternoon job. Keep the hose fully uncoiled to avoid kinks.
products.bestFor: Strong electric cleaning with no engine upkeep.
pros: Independent lab verified pressure and flow
No fuel, oil or spark plug
cons: Flow is a maximum, below gas washers

products.name: Tecoloy 2200 PSI 3.2 GPM Commercial Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The Tecoloy is an unusual electric: a permanent magnet inverter motor of about 3 HP driving a horizontal triplex pump, with a stated 3.2 GPM maximum at 2200 PSI. Triplex plunger pumps are the commercial standard because they are durable and serviceable, which is a real upgrade over the sealed axial pumps in consumer machines.

Flow is the big number. At maximum it gives about 7,040 cleaning units, close to the gas machines, with a claimed noise of 65 dB. The catch is that such a motor draws far more power than a household 15 amp circuit may supply, so check the listing for its electrical requirements before you buy.

A triplex pump needs periodic oil changes, and you should winterize it. It is the choice for someone who wants gas-class flow without exhaust, and who has the right power. Treat the electrical requirement as the first purchase decision, because a washer you cannot power is a paperweight. Maintain the pump oil on schedule and use a surge-protected supply.
products.bestFor: High flow without an engine, if you have the power supply.

products.name: DeWalt 3000 PSI 1.1 GPM 15 Amp Cold Water Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The DeWalt electric states 3000 PSI at 1.1 GPM on a 15 amp circuit, giving about 3,300 cleaning units. That is less than half the Greenworks's maximum flow, so the pressure headline is more impressive than the cleaning speed.

Its selling points are the DeWalt name and internal storage for the accessories. The listing provides limited detail, so confirm the specification before you buy.

Drain it for winter. It suits a buyer who wants a known brand in an electric. Compared with the Greenworks, you gain a known brand but give up flow, so pick it only if the name and storage matter to you. Confirm the listing details before you buy.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a branded electric with storage.

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3000e 3000 Max PSI Induction Motor Washer
products.description:
The WPX3000e is the mid-tier electric in this list, with a rated 2600 PSI at 1.1 GPM and an induction motor. It is the machine to buy if the gas and high-flow electrics are more than you need.

Its rated pair gives about 2,860 cleaning units, a fraction of the gas washers' figures, but it is quiet and easy to own.

Drain the pump for winter. Compared with the gas washers, this one is quieter and lighter, but it will not strip a driveway quickly. It is the right tool for a household that wants a sturdy electric for decks, siding and vehicles.
products.bestFor: Electric users who do not need gas-class flow.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cleaning units are PSI times GPM. The DeWalt gas washer gives about 7,920, the Westinghouse gas washer about 8,840, and the WPX3000e about 2,860. Flow often sets cleaning speed more than the pressure headline, so choose the machine with the flow your area needs. Check the hose length and quality, because a short hose forces you to move a heavy machine often.

Gas engines supply the horsepower for 2.4 to 2.6 GPM. Electrics max out near 2 GPM on household power. Gas needs fuel, oil and upkeep, while electrics need only a drain for winter. Choose gas for large surfaces. Keep the machine on level ground and avoid running it in a closed garage because of exhaust.

The gas machines use axial cam pumps, which are economical but not rebuildable, while the Tecoloy uses a horizontal triplex pump that is serviceable. Triplex pumps last longer and need periodic oil changes. For occasional use an axial pump is fine. Find out how local rules treat wash water, since runoff from degreasers may be restricted.

The engine must be able to drive the pump. A 208cc engine at 3300 PSI and 2.4 GPM, or a 212cc engine at 3400 PSI and 2.6 GPM, are plausible matches. Be wary of any claim far above what the engine size suggests. Look for pneumatic tires and a folding handle if you will move it over grass.

The Greenworks says its pressure and flow were verified by an independent lab, and the WPX3000e states rated figures. Prefer verified or rated numbers to peaks. Compare the warranty on the pump and engine separately.

The Tecoloy uses a permanent magnet inverter motor of about 3 HP. Check the electrical requirements, since a household 15 amp circuit may not suffice. Think about storage: a gas washer must be stored upright with stabilized fuel.

howWeEvaluated.description: We computed PSI times GPM from stated figures. The Westinghouse gas washer led at about 8,840, followed by the DeWalt at about 7,920. Flow carried the most weight because it decides cleaning speed on large surfaces.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pump and engine
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pump type and engine size. The triplex pump on the Tecoloy scored high for serviceability. Pump type and engine match were checked for plausibility.

howWeEvaluated.description: We credited verified and rated figures and discounted maximums. Verified and rated figures earned more credit than maximums.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed fuel, oil and winterizing against the convenience of electric. Ownership costs, such as fuel and oil changes, were counted against gas machines.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The DeWalt and Westinghouse gas washers move 2.4 to 2.6 GPM and clean concrete in minutes, but need fuel, oil changes and hearing protection.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: The Greenworks, WPX3000e and DeWalt electric are quiet and low maintenance, but their flow is much lower.

howToChoose.note: Pick gas for large surfaces; pick electric for convenience and light work.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least 2.4 GPM of flow and a surface cleaner attachment if you can. Flow sets the speed on concrete more than the pressure headline.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The two gas washers are the best fits, with the Tecoloy the quiet electric alternative if you can supply its power.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You wash for a living or need a triplex gas machine with a commercial engine. Those sit above this cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash cars and furniture. A lower tier covers it.

maintenance.why: Gas engines need clean oil to protect bearings. Use fresh fuel and store the machine upright.
Stale fuel gums the carburetor. Run the pump only with water attached and the trigger open for startup.

maintenance.task: Clean the air filter and check the plug
maintenance.why: A clogged filter or worn plug causes hard starts.
Frozen water can crack the pump. Run pump antifreeze through it.

faq.a: For large surfaces, yes, because flow is far higher. For cars and light work, electric is simpler and quieter. Large surfaces need flow more than pressure.

faq.q: Can I run the Tecoloy on a normal outlet?
faq.a: Check its electrical requirements. A motor of about 3 HP may need more than a standard 15 amp circuit. Always check the plug and circuit requirements first.

faq.q: What safety gear do I need?
faq.a: Eye and hearing protection, closed shoes, and never point the spray at people or pets. High-pressure water can penetrate skin. A wide stance and steady hands help when starting the wand.
